To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
adolescents' perceptions of foods differ from those of adults.
(a) students from different backgrounds and different ages had different perceptions of the same foods; and (b) these perceptions were related to their social and personal characteristics.
the foods that secondary students and tertiary dietetic and health students rated as their Favourite and Disliked were similar, and that the ways in which they construed the foods were different.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways students construe their Favourite and Disliked foods.
the way adolescents think about food.
the ways adolescents construe food, and the factors that influence their perceptions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
adolescents' perceptions of their Favourite foods are not very different from their perceptions of their Disliked foods.
students' conceptions are not only influenced by age, sex, ethnicity and educational level, but also by the social and economic environment in which the students live.

the foods that students liked and disliked were those that were perceived to be "fattening-poor', and those that were "healthy', and that the differences in students' perceptions of foods were due to age, gender, ethnicity, and the educational level of the students.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adolescents have a more positive attitude towards foods that are high in fat, sugar and salt and that this is not related to gender, age or ethnic background.
the most important factors for students in choosing foods are the social aspects.
the most important factors in the students' perceptions of food are the social and cultural aspects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the food choices made by adolescents are not simply a function of their biological needs, but also a reflection of their social environment, and their social motivations.
the foods students choose to eat and dislike are not as simple as we think they might be.
we need to understand the social motivations for food choices, as well as the individual and cultural influences on those choices.
